info.title: MVP Site
info.description: MVP-site example app: aggregates the site (miners, a powermeter, a mining pool) via the MDK protocol client.

get.description: Live site snapshot assembled from `telemetry.pull` across all workers: all miners, site power consumption from powermeters, and pool data from all minerpool workers. Workers that are down are listed in `unavailableWorkers` with their device counts, since their devices cannot be read.

200.description: Live site snapshot: miners, site power, and pools.

400.description: The request cannot be served as sent.

get.description: Historical telemetry from the workers' persisted tail-logs (`telemetry.pull` type `logs`). `metric=hashrate` reads pool stats-history (H/s, the unit the pool contracts declare; all pools summed by default; pass `deviceId` for one pool). `metric=site-hashrate` reads the miners' own snap tail-logs summed across all miners (MH/s; pass `deviceId` for one miner). `metric=power` reads site powermeter series (all meters summed by default; pass `deviceId` for one meter). `metric=temperature` reads sensor tail-logs, averaged by default; this example ships no sensor Worker, so it returns empty unless one is added. Defaults to the last hour.

200.description: Historical time-series read from a worker tail-log.

post.description: Dispatches the `setupPools` capability command to a single miner through Kernel. Pools from the request body take precedence; with no body the site-wide default from `config/site.deploy.json` (`worker.pools`) is applied. The miner reboots to pick up the new pools, so expect it to drop offline briefly.

bearer.description: An access token from the Gateway's `/auth/login`, `/auth/token` or `/auth/refresh`. Each operation's role name is its `spec.rbac` requirement: the verb and resource a rule must grant the caller.

GatewayError.description: The body of every error the Gateway answers.

error.description: The HTTP status text, such as `Unauthorized`.

message.description: The `ERR_*` code, followed by a colon, a space, and a detail when there is one. For a body the Gateway cannot read, or a request that fails the route's schema, Fastify's message. Otherwise, the HTTP status text.

HostNotAllowed.description: The Gateway does not serve the request's host.

x-mdk-errors.description: The request's `Host` header is missing, or names a host the Gateway does not serve. The Gateway serves loopback on its port, its own bind address, and each `allowedHosts` entry. With `trustProxy` set, `X-Forwarded-Host` is checked instead.
x-mdk-errors.fix: Call the Gateway by a host it serves, or have the operator add the host to `allowedHosts`.

RateLimited.description: The caller has sent too many requests.

x-mdk-errors.description: The caller's address has sent more requests than the Gateway's `rateLimit` allows in its time window, `300` a minute by default.
x-mdk-errors.fix: Wait for the time window to pass, then retry.

Unauthorized.description: The Gateway could not authenticate the caller.

x-mdk-errors.description: The request carries no bearer token, or one that fails verification, such as an expired or revoked token.
x-mdk-errors.fix: Sign in, and send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

VerifierRefused.description: On a Gateway with no RBAC authority, an `auth: true` route runs the operator's `authVerifier` after the rate limit and before the body is read, in place of authentication and authorization. The route answers the verifier's own `4xx` error when it throws one whose message starts with `ERR_`. Otherwise it answers `401` `ERR_AUTH_UNAUTHORIZED`: when none is configured, when the verifier refuses the caller, and when it throws anything else. The operator who supplies the verifier documents its codes, and the `@tetherto/mdk-gateway` README describes the hook.
VerifierRefused.x-mdk-fix: Send the credentials the operator's verifier expects.

MediaTypeUnsupported.description: A request other than `GET` carries a body in a content type the Gateway has no parser for; it parses `application/json` and `text/plain`. The Gateway reads the body after the rate limit and the caller's authentication or custom verifier, and before authorization. The message is Fastify's `Unsupported Media Type`, not an `ERR_*` code.
MediaTypeUnsupported.x-mdk-fix: Send the body in the content type the operation declares.

BodyTooLarge.description: A request other than `GET` carries a body larger than the Gateway's `bodyLimit`, `1048576` bytes by default. The Gateway reads the body after the rate limit and the caller's authentication or custom verifier, and before authorization. The message is Fastify's `Request body is too large`, not an `ERR_*` code.
BodyTooLarge.x-mdk-fix: Send a smaller body, or have the operator raise `bodyLimit`.

BodyMalformed.description: A request other than `GET` carries a body that does not parse as its content type, such as malformed JSON, or an empty body sent as `application/json`. The Gateway reads the body after the rate limit and the caller's authentication or custom verifier, and before authorization. The message is Fastify's parse error, not an `ERR_*` code.
BodyMalformed.x-mdk-fix: Send a body that parses as its `Content-Type`.

Forbidden.description: The caller may not make this call.

RequestInvalid.description: The request's path parameters, query, or body fail the schema the app's route table declares for the route. The message is Fastify's validation error, not an `ERR_*` code.
RequestInvalid.x-mdk-fix: Send the parameters and body the operation declares.

AppRuntimeBadGateway.description: The Gateway could not reach the app runtime, or could not read its answer.

x-mdk-errors.description: The app runtime answered in a different protocol version from the Gateway's client.
x-mdk-errors.fix: Run the Gateway and the app runtime from the same MDK release.

x-mdk-errors.description: The app runtime is unreachable, does not allow the Gateway's key, or closed or garbled its reply.
x-mdk-errors.fix: Check that the app runtime is running and allows the Gateway's key, then retry. A call that changes something may have run before its reply was lost, so check its result first.

AppRuntimeNotStarted.description: The app runtime is not serving yet.

x-mdk-errors.description: The app runtime has not published its key file: it has not started yet, or it has stopped.
x-mdk-errors.fix: Start the app runtime, or retry once it has started.

AppRuntimeTimeout.description: The app runtime did not answer in time.

x-mdk-errors.description: The app runtime sent no answer, or no stream head, within the Gateway's `appTimeoutMs`, `60000` by default. The Gateway stops waiting, but the route's controller is not stopped, so the call may still complete.
x-mdk-errors.fix: Retry a call that only reads. For a call that changes something, check its result or the device's state before sending it again. If it repeats, check the route's controller, or raise `appTimeoutMs`.

ControllerError.description: An error the route's controller throws arrives with its `statusCode` when that is `400` or more, else `403` for `ERR_KERNEL_ACTION_FORBIDDEN` (the Kernel refused the call under `spec.rbac`), `400` for any other `ERR_*` error, and `500` for anything else. A message that does not start with `ERR_` arrives as the status text, such as `Internal Server Error`, and the app runtime logs the original. The app's route table declares the codes its controllers throw.
ControllerError.x-mdk-fix: Act on the code as the operation declares it.

KernelClientError.description: A controller that passes on an error from its Kernel client relays the client's `ERR_*` code, which arrives as `400` by the controller rule, or `403` for `ERR_KERNEL_ACTION_FORBIDDEN`. The `@tetherto/mdk-client` README documents the client's transport codes, and the `@tetherto/mdk-kernel` README the Kernel's refusals.
KernelClientError.x-mdk-fix: Act on the code as the package that throws it documents.
